outcomes: Framework backends apply one reusable timeout rule to bounded request operations
A context detached from caller cancellation receives a new deadline before it reaches a dependency
Callers can defer the returned cancel function for every timeout configuration
nonGoals: Detaching a context from its caller
Bounding streaming response bodies whose lifetime extends past the helper call

requirements.text: WithRequestTimeout re-installs a deadline on a context whose own deadline context.WithoutCancel stripped, so detached bounded work still fails closed instead of running unbounded.
A zero or negative timeout returns the original context and a safe no-op cancel function.
A positive timeout returns context.WithTimeout derived from the supplied context and preserves its values.
